But no criminalisation of trans identity, no imprisonment documented. I'd say 0.38.

Dossier 2: Same-sex conduct not criminalised. No documented anti-trans violence. Official posture hostile: cabinet decision targeting LGBTQIA+ activities, committee drafting policy banning LGBTQIA+ advocacy/promotion, marriage amendment. Conservative social climate, advised to avoid PDA, no gay scene. Prosecutorial guidance treats SOGI hostility as aggravating factor — a real protection (climate). No anti-discrimination law generally. No documented universal exposures, no documented targeting of trans visitors, no violence record. The 2024 advocacy ban is directed at advocacy/promotion — could reach a visibly trans visitor? It's a policy direction, unsourced enforcement. Threat-framing from state (tier: official hostility but aimed at advocacy). Thin data. Social conservatism but no documented hostility incidents. I'd rate around 0.45-0.50. Compared to Dossier 1: dossier 1 has documented police extortion and documented violence. Dossier 2 has state anti-LGBTQ policy direction but no documented violence or police abuse. Hmm. State threat-framing is significant. The prosecutorial guidance is a genuine protective factor for crime victims. No criminalisation. I'd say 0.48.

Dossier 3: Strong protections: border accepts foreign documents and X markers, no extra gender documents; discrimination prohibited in employment, housing, accommodations; hate crime aggravating factor; bathroom access protected; high public acceptance (91% same rights); marriage equality. Negatives: rising reports of discrimination (4,800 reports, trans reports up 51%), only six convictions; detention placement with no governing rule — frequently Extra Care wing alongside sex offenders, documented cases of men's wing placement. But detention only matters if traveler detained — a tier 1 exposure but low probability for a visitor. The survey: 17% of transgender people experienced physical/sexual violence (official figure) — no denominator comparison but it's a trans-specific prevalence figure. Rising discrimination reports. Pride incidents 25-45. Overall this is a low-risk jurisdiction with documented protections operating (Safer Spaces, mayor action, compensation). Detention placement gap is real but case-by-case with preference considered. Score ~0.82-0.85. Given detention practice uncertainty and rising discrimination reports with only six convictions, maybe 0.80.

Dossier 4: No criminalisation (since 1995). Comprehensive anti-discrimination law covering SO in goods/services etc. — note: covers sexual orientation, and 2020 expansion to sex characteristics and HIV; hate crime amendment covers sexual orientation and gender identity (2013). 2013 law punishing dissemination of homophobic information. Enforcement uneven: slow complaints, official making pathologizing remarks. 2016 removal of SOGI from Constitution. No same-sex marriage. Social attitudes hostile (56% shouldn't show preferences publicly, 55% no homosexual neighbors, 9.3% accept LGBT doctor). Ten bias-motivated violence cases against trans people logged in one year (raw count, no denominator). UN expert visited 2024. Legal gender recognition unresolved. So: legal protections exist (hate crime covering GI, anti-discrimination covering... does the ADL cover gender identity? It says covers sexual orientation in employment, goods/services... expanded to sex characteristics and HIV. Not explicitly gender identity. Hmm — "covers sexual orientation" only. Hate crime amendment covers gender identity). Visitor-facing: no criminalisation, no universal exposure, hate-crime protection covering GI, but societal hostility documented at scale and enforcement slow/uneven. Violence: 10 cases/year trans-specific logged by a community group — no denominator but that's a modest number. Score ~0.55-0.60. Social hostility is tier 3 with thin/slow recourse. Protections exist but poorly enforced. I'd say 0.57.

Compare dossier 1 vs 4: Dossier 1 has police extortion using ambiguous statute (tier 2 state-tolerated targeting), documented violence by state and non-state actors, 73% hostility, no protections at all. Dossier 4 has hate crime law covering GI, AD law, but hostile social attitudes and slow enforcement, small violence count. Dossier 1 should be lower. Dossier 1: 0.36; Dossier 4: 0.55.

Dossier 5: Criminalisation of same-sex conduct (3mo-2yr), no legal gender recognition, police/prosecutors refuse to investigate crimes against LGBTQ+, dozens imprisoned under pretext charges (uncorroborated), official hostility, hostile social attitudes (15% think good place for gay/lesbian), LGBTQ hiding identity, healthcare discrimination, 2013 arrests. This is high risk: criminalisation plus no recourse plus state-tolerated impunity. Trans visitor outed — relationship read as same-sex falls within statute; police refuse to investigate crimes against them. Not organized targeting campaign documented with arrests for mere presence, but refusal of recourse + criminalisation. Score ~0.25-0.30. The "dozens imprisoned under pretext" is uncorroborated but from civil society. No trans-specific violence stats. Criminal statute with enforcement history (2013 arrests, 2017 adoption by 111-1). Police refusal to investigate crimes against LGBTQ is severe — victim has no recourse. I'd say 0.27.

4: 0.56
